sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. In P. K. Austin & S. McGill (eds.) Language Documentation and Description 11, 90-135. London: SOAS.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/documentation survey. Table of existing documentation lists 'Shiroro: Tarin (Pongu/Pangu) — Unpublished grammatical sketch (MacDonell 2007)'. No phonology of Pongu; only prosodic remark is generic (NW Kainji languages range 'from languages with extremely short lexemes with highly complex tonal systems to languages with long phonological words and restricted tone systems', p.92). No stress statement.

sources.citation: MacDonell, James (facilitator). 2009. Azha̱a̱zha̱a̱ na Ri (Names of things). Basic word book. Kagara: Tuma na Ta̱rin. 13 pp.
sources.note: Picture vocabulary in the practical orthography; no accents, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: MacDonell, James (facilitator). 2008. Yadda za a karanta a kuma rubuta Panganci / How to read and write Pangu (for those who read Hausa). Trial edition. Kagara: Tuma na Ta̱rin. 24 pp.
sources.note: Transition primer. Section 8 'Ƙarin alamomin fahinta' (pp.14-15) prescribes an acute accent on the first vowel of a verb to mark action at a distant place (Nʼnii kúshe̱ vs Nʼnii kúushe̱) and vowel doubling for 2nd-person-object/benefactive forms: grammatical tone/length marking, not stress. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Dettweiler, Stephen & Sonia Dettweiler. 2002. Sociolinguistic survey of the Pongu people. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-040. 29 pp.
sources.note: No phonology section; three 170-item wordlists (appendix B, scanned images; one page scanned) show noun-class prefixes and sporadic acute accents without a legend. Nothing on stress; the only 'stress' hit is the verb 'it should be stressed'.
